<!-- Portrait: /assets/img/portrait.jpg (192×192, shown at 96 px) arrives with owner item O2; until then this margin column stays empty. -->

I study the step between estimating a characteristic-based factor model and using it to choose stock holdings: how the inputs to an investment rule, not only the model's forecasts, shape what an investor ends up holding. Figure 1 draws one such input, the geometry of 132 stock characteristics, month by month from June 1973 to November 2024.[^hero]

My job market paper, [Characteristic Libraries and Portfolio Decisions](/research/characteristic-libraries.qmd), shows that repeating or rescaling existing stock characteristics can change a tuned investment rule without adding information. [Characteristic Geometry and Portfolio Choice](/research/characteristic-geometry.qmd) finds that nearly identical forecasts generate different portfolios because a fixed adjustment to factor variances imposes different exposure penalties across measurement conventions; removing this adjustment nearly eliminates the weight gap. [Characteristic-Space Metrics in Factor Models](/research/characteristic-space-metrics.qmd) starts from the fact that characteristic-based factor models can fit returns identically while attributing them differently to latent, observed-factor, and intercept components, and shows how an inner product on characteristic space selects this decomposition. Both working papers grow out of my PhD thesis, [No-Arbitrage IPCA](/research/no-arbitrage-ipca.qmd), which develops a framework for geometry-aware asset pricing in high-dimensional characteristic spaces.

[^hero]: **How Figure 1 encodes the metric.** For month $t$, let $s_t$ be the top-eigenvalue share and $d_t$ the participation dimension of the 132×132 rolling characteristic Gram metric, and let $u_t = \min\{1, \max\{0, (s_t - 0.1176)/(0.1521 - 0.1176)\}\}$ and $v_t = \min\{1, \max\{0, (d_t - 17.36)/(22.63 - 17.36)\}\}$, where the bounds are the sample minimum and maximum over the 618 months. Then $\text{ratio}_t = 1.4 + 2.6\,u_t$, $\text{size}_t = 0.85 + 0.30\,v_t$, $\lambda_1 = \text{size}_t\sqrt{\text{ratio}_t}$ and $\lambda_2 = \text{size}_t/\sqrt{\text{ratio}_t}$. The ellipse is the unit ball of $M_t = \operatorname{diag}(\lambda_1^2, \lambda_2^2)$, with semi-axes $1/\lambda_1$ and $1/\lambda_2$; the spoke at angle $\varphi$ has length $\sqrt{\lambda_1^2\cos^2\varphi + \lambda_2^2\sin^2\varphi}$; under the identity ruler every spoke has length 1. Data: `Characteristic_Geometry_and_Portfolio_Choice_Research_Release_2026-09-09/02_Presentation/Source/data/rolling_geometry.csv`; recession months from `03_Replication/modules/business_cycles/nber_monthly.csv` in the same release.
